title: Scaffolding owns placement and boundaries; Backend Composition owns what is inside the layers
subject: main
summary: Scaffolding & Import Boundaries owns where code lives and who may reach whom. Backend Composition owns what happens inside the layers: entities, model ownership

adr.context: The Reference of [[scaffolding-and-import-boundaries|Scaffolding & Import Boundaries]] had been filled by an agent pulling every standard it judged relevant. It carried entity, model and schema rules — but Backend Composition's first axiom is already "every entity has exactly one schema definition across slices and apps", and that doc has a written Model Ownership section. Two docs were claiming one subject.
adr.decision: Scaffolding & Import Boundaries owns where code lives and who may reach whom. Backend Composition owns what happens inside the layers: entities, model ownership, layer responsibilities, list contracts, external-provider adapters. The general sharing principle — shared code sits at the nearest level above all its consumers — stays in Scaffolding, with schemas appearing there only as an example of it.
consequences: SCF2, SCF3, SCF4, SCF5, SCF6, SCF7, SCF9, SCF13, API33 and PRV1 were un-consumed from Scaffolding and point at Backend Composition in the tracker. SCF1 stays: the fixed folder shape of every slice is scaffolding; what lives inside the folders is layering.
AC44 has no destination: it governs how every doc is enforced, and the DOC/PRC rules have no target document in the mind map.
Scaffolding's Reference went from six blocks and 26 claims to five blocks and roughly half that.
Some rules are consumed without a reference claim: MOD6 and MOD9 by the axioms, MOD11 by the Purpose (decoupability), MOD8 by the glossary (its content is the library and seed slice definitions).

`backend-composition` and `access-control` were created carrying axioms and purpose only, with an empty Reference: the division has to be visible for either doc to stay honest, but filling a Reference nobody has reviewed would fake a digestion that has not happened.
